99: +// applyLinkImpairments sets the link impairments of the given endpoints on their interfaces.
100: +// Impairments don't survive moving an interface to another namespace, so they have to be set
101: +// again whenever the interfaces of a node are restored.
102: +func applyLinkImpairments(ctx context.Context, endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint) error {
103: +	var errs []error
104: +	moduleLoaded := false
105: +
106: +	for _, endpoint := range endpoints {
107: +		netem := endpoint.GetNetem()
108: +		if netem == nil {
109: +			continue
110: +		}
111: +
112: +		if !moduleLoaded {
113: +			loadNetemModule(ctx)
114: +			moduleLoaded = true
115: +		}
116: +
117: +		if err := applyEndpointImpairment(ctx, endpoint, netem); err != nil {
118: +			errs = append(
119: +				errs,
120: +				fmt.Errorf("failed to set the link impairment of %s: %w", endpoint, err),
121: +			)
122: +		}
123: +	}
124: +
125: +	return errors.Join(errs...)

128: +func applyEndpointImpairment(
129: +	ctx context.Context,
130: +	endpoint clablinks.Endpoint,
131: +	netem *clablinks.Netem,
132: +) error {
133: +	node := endpoint.GetNode()
134: +
135: +	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
136: +		nodeNS, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
137: +		if err != nil {
138: +			return err
139: +		}
140: +		defer nodeNS.Close()
141: +
142: +		tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNS.Fd()))
143: +		if err != nil {
144: +			return err
145: +		}
146: +		defer func() {
147: +			if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
148: +				log.Debugf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
149: +			}
150: +		}()
151: +
152: +		link, err := net.InterfaceByName(endpoint.GetIfaceName())
153: +		if err != nil {
154: +			return err
155: +		}
156: +
157: +		if err := clabnetem.ReplaceImpairments(
158: +			tcnl,
159: +			link,
160: +			netem.Delay,
161: +			netem.Jitter,
162: +			netem.Loss,
163: +			netem.Rate,
164: +			netem.Corruption,
165: +		); err != nil {
166: +			return err
167: +		}
168: +
169: +		log.Info(
170: +			"Set link impairments",
171: +			"node", node.GetShortName(),
172: +			"interface", endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
173: +		)
174: +
175: +		return nil
176: +	})
177: +}

226: @@ -16,5 +16,47 @@ Labs are meant to be a reflection of real-world scenarios. To make simulated net
227:  These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.
228:  
229:  ```bash title="setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node"
230:  containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10
231:  ```
232: +
233: +## Impairments in the topology
234: +
235: +Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:
236: +
237: +```yaml
238: +topology:
239: +  links:
240: +    - type: veth
241: +      endpoints:
242: +        - node: r1
243: +          interface: eth1
244: +          netem:
245: +            delay: 50ms
246: +            jitter: 5ms
247: +            loss: 0.5
248: +        - node: r2
249: +          interface: eth1
250: +          netem:
251: +            rate: 10000
252: +```
253: +
254: +| Key          | Meaning                                                               |
255: +| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
256: +| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |
257: +| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |
258: +| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |
259: +| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |
260: +| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |
261: +
262: +Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:
263: +
264: +```yaml
265: +topology:
266: +  links:
267: +    - endpoints: ["r1:eth1", "r2:eth1"]
268: +      netem:
269: +        - delay: 50ms
270: +        - {}
271: +```
272: +
273: +Impairments are supported on veth links. Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

482: +package links
483: +
484: +import (
485: +	"fmt"
486: +	"math"
487: +	"time"
488: +)
489: +
490: +// maxNetemJitter is the highest jitter the kernel accepts without capping it.
491: +const maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond
492: +
493: +// maxNetemRate is the highest rate in kbit/s that can be converted to bytes/s.
494: +const maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64 / 1000
495: +
496: +// NetemRaw is the link impairment of an endpoint as defined in the topology file.
497: +// It applies to the packets the endpoint's interface sends.
498: +type NetemRaw struct {
499: +	Delay      string  `yaml:"delay,omitempty"`
500: +	Jitter     string  `yaml:"jitter,omitempty"`
501: +	Loss       float64 `yaml:"loss,omitempty"`
502: +	Rate       uint64  `yaml:"rate,omitempty"`
503: +	Corruption float64 `yaml:"corruption,omitempty"`
504: +}
505: +
506: +// Netem is the resolved link impairment of an endpoint.
507: +type Netem struct {
508: +	Delay      time.Duration
509: +	Jitter     time.Duration
510: +	Loss       float64
511: +	Rate       uint64
512: +	Corruption float64
513: +}
514: +
515: +// Resolve validates the impairment and returns nil if it sets nothing.
516: +func (r *NetemRaw) Resolve() (*Netem, error) {
517: +	if r == nil {
518: +		return nil, nil
519: +	}
520: +
521: +	netem := &Netem{Loss: r.Loss, Rate: r.Rate, Corruption: r.Corruption}
522: +
523: +	var err error
524: +	if netem.Delay, err = parseNetemDuration("delay", r.Delay); err != nil {
525: +		return nil, err
526: +	}
527: +	if netem.Jitter, err = parseNetemDuration("jitter", r.Jitter); err != nil {
528: +		return nil, err
529: +	}
530: +
531: +	if netem.Jitter != 0 && netem.Delay == 0 {
532: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter cannot be set without setting delay")
533: +	}
534: +	if netem.Jitter > maxNetemJitter {
535: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter must be at most %s", maxNetemJitter)
536: +	}
537: +	if !(netem.Loss >= 0 && netem.Loss <= 100) {
538: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem loss must be in the range between 0 and 100")
539: +	}
540: +	if !(netem.Corruption >= 0 && netem.Corruption <= 100) {
541: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem corruption must be in the range between 0 and 100")
542: +	}
543: +
544: +	if netem.Rate > maxNetemRate {
545: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem rate must be at most %d kbit/s", uint64(maxNetemRate))
546: +	}
547: +
548: +	if *netem == (Netem{}) {
549: +		return nil, nil
550: +	}
551: +
552: +	return netem, nil
553: +}
554: +
555: +func parseNetemDuration(name, value string) (time.Duration, error) {
556: +	if value == "" {
557: +		return 0, nil
558: +	}
559: +
560: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
561: +	if err != nil {
562: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q is not a duration, e.g. 100ms: %w", name, value, err)
563: +	}
564: +	if duration < 0 {
565: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q must not be negative", name, value)
566: +	}
567: +
568: +	return duration, nil
569: +}

# Karpathy behavioral guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:

- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:

- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:

- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

---

**These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

59: func ReplaceImpairments(tcnl *tc.Tc, link *net.Interface, delay, jitter time.Duration,
60: 	loss float64, rate uint64, probability float64,
61: ) error {
62: 	err := tcnl.SetOption(netlink.ExtendedAcknowledge, true)
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return fmt.Errorf("could not set option ExtendedAcknowledge: %v", err)
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	qdisc := tc.Object{
68: 		Msg: tc.Msg{
69: 			Family:  unix.AF_UNSPEC,
70: 			Ifindex: uint32(link.Index),
71: 			Handle:  core.BuildHandle(0x1, 0x0),
72: 			Parent:  tc.HandleRoot,
73: 			Info:    0,
74: 		},
75: 		Attribute: tc.Attribute{
76: 			Kind: "netem",
77: 			Netem: &tc.Netem{
78: 				Qopt: tc.NetemQopt{
79: 					Limit: 10000, // max number of packets netem can hold during delay
80: 				},
81: 			},
82: 		},
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	setDelay(&qdisc, delay, jitter)
86: 
87: 	setLoss(&qdisc, loss)
88: 
89: 	setRate(&qdisc, rate)
90: 
91: 	// Always set the corruption field (even if probability is 0) to allow resetting.
92: 	setCorruption(&qdisc, probability)
93: 
94: 	return tcnl.Qdisc().Replace(&qdisc)

99: 	qdisc := tc.Object{
100: 		Msg: tc.Msg{
101: 			Family:  unix.AF_UNSPEC,
102: 			Ifindex: uint32(link.Index),
103: 			Handle:  core.BuildHandle(0x1, 0x0),
104: 			Parent:  tc.HandleRoot,
105: 			Info:    0,
106: 		},
107: 		Attribute: tc.Attribute{
108: 			Kind:  "netem",
109: 			Netem: &tc.Netem{},
110: 		},
111: 	}

115: // setDelay sets delay and jitter to the qdisc.
116: func setDelay(qdisc *tc.Object, delay, jitter time.Duration) {
117: 	delayNs := delay.Nanoseconds()
118: 	jitterNs := jitter.Nanoseconds()

120: 	qdisc.Attribute.Netem.Latency64 = &delayNs
121: 	qdisc.Attribute.Netem.Jitter64 = &jitterNs

124: // setLoss sets the loss to the qdisc.

126: 	qdisc.Attribute.Netem.Qopt.Loss = uint32(math.Round(math.MaxUint32 * (loss / float64(100))))

129: // setRate sets the rate to the qdisc.
130: // The rate is provided in kbit.
131: func setRate(qdisc *tc.Object, rate uint64) {
132: 	// convert to bytes
133: 	byteRate := rate * 1000 / 8
134: 	qdisc.Attribute.Netem.Rate = &tc.NetemRate{
135: 		Rate: uint32(min(byteRate, math.MaxUint32)),
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	if byteRate > math.MaxUint32 {
139: 		qdisc.Attribute.Netem.Rate64 = &byteRate
140: 	}
141: }

144: func setCorruption(qdisc *tc.Object, probability float64) {
145: 	qdisc.Netem.Corrupt = &tc.NetemCorrupt{
146: 		Probability: uint32(math.Round(math.MaxUint32 * (probability / float64(100)))),
147: 	}

153: 	if err != nil {
154: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not get all qdiscs: %v", err)
155: 	}

292: 			return idx, nil

294: 	}

For an extended veth link with an endpoint `node: host` (is that possible? params.Nodes contains "host" per core/clab.go line 901 `"host": clablinks.GetHostLinkNode()`). Yes! So an extended veth link can have `node: host` endpoint. If the user puts netem on the host endpoint (schema allows it — link-endpoint is shared), applyLinkImpairments would run in the ROOT netns and set a netem qdisc on an arbitrary host interface (e.g., eth0 on the host machine!). Wait — endpoint.GetIfaceName() for the host endpoint is the interface the user named. So `netem` on a `host:` endpoint of an extended veth link → apply netem qdisc to a host interface in the root namespace. The doc says impairments are supported on veth links (implying any veth link endpoint). But for brief links, host endpoints are explicitly rejected with "netem is only supported on veth links, not on host links". The inconsistency: brief rejects host endpoint netem, extended allows it — silently impairing a host interface in the root netns. That is a real inconsistency/footgun introduced by this PR: the guard exists only in `ToTypeSpecificRawLink` (brief path), not for extended links. Severity: P2/P3? Impact: user can accidentally impair host networking; inconsistent validation. The brief-link error message says netem only supported on veth links, but the same schema-valid config on an extended link is silently accepted. Also macvlan/mgmt-net brief rejection vs extended acceptance.

Hmm wait, actually for brief links, can an endpoint be `host:` inside a brief veth link? `parseLinkType("host")` → LinkTypeHost → hostLinkFromBrief — the brief form is type-agnostic; the type is determined by the special endpoint. So a brief link `["r1:eth1", "host:eth0"]` IS a host link, not veth. Right — brief links with host endpoints are host links by definition. So the netem rejection for host brief links is correct: "not on host links". And the doc statement "Impairments are supported on veth links" — for extended links, `type: veth` with `node: host` endpoint — is that a thing? Let me check whether extended veth links support host endpoints... `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` calls `epr.Resolve(params, l)` which uses node.GetLinkEndpointType() → host → NewEndpointHost. So yes, extended veth links support host endpoints (that's the documented extended form of host links? Actually docs say host links are `type: host` with `host-interface`. But `node: host` in extended veth also works I think).

So: schema allows netem on any `link-endpoint` (including within `link-type-host`? let me check — link-type-host has `endpoint` $ref link-endpoint). So a user could set netem in `type: host` link's endpoint — applied to the node's interface in node netns — fine.

The real risk: netem on the `host` node's endpoint (extended veth) → qdisc on host root-ns interface. Is that harmful? It modifies host networking state. It's opt-in and arguably even a feature (impair host-side of the veth). Hmm, it's symmetric with `tools netem set -n <host?...>`. Actually `tools netem set` requires a node name from the lab; can it target the host? Let me check tools_netem.go. If tools netem can't target host, then topology netem applying to host is inconsistent.

Let me not overweight this. The primary observable inconsistency: brief link `["r1:eth1", "mgmt-net:br0"]` with netem → error; extended `type: mgmt-net` with netem on endpoint → silently applied to container interface (works fine actually). MaxUint64/1000 = 18446744073709551 (integer division: 18446744073709551615/1000 = 18446744073709551.615 → floor 18446744073709551). Code: `maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64 / 1000` = 18446744073709551. W. Now `core/apply.go` empty-plan path: it calls applyLinkImpairments BEFORE finalize — but note when `plan.empty()` and the node is stopped... Let me check planApply handling of stopped nodes to decide. Let me search topology_reconcile.go for "state" or "running".

And when plan is NOT empty (e.g., added link), impairments applied for all c.Links endpoints. OK.

## Objective

## Important Details
- PR adds per-endpoint link impairments (netem) feature: new `NetemRaw`/`Netem` in `links/netem.go`, applied via new `core/link_netem.go` (`applyLinkImpairments`, `applyEndpointImpairment`, `linksEndpoints`), called from `core/apply.go` (both empty-plan and non-empty-plan paths), `core/deploy.go`, `core/start.go`, `core/restart.go`.
- 21 changed paths: M `.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml`, `core/apply.go`, `core/deploy.go`, `core/restart.go`, `core/start.go`, `docs/manual/impairments.md`, `docs/manual/topo-def-file.md`, `links/endpoint.go`, `links/endpoint_raw.go`, `links/link_brief.go`, `links/link_veth.go`, `netem/netem.go`, `schemas/clab.schema.json`, `schemas/schema_test.go`; A `core/link_netem.go`, `links/netem.go`, `links/netem_test.go`, `tests/01-smoke/34-link-netem.clab.yml`, `tests/01-smoke/34-link-netem.robot`, plus 2 more truncated paths in manifest.json (consult when needed).
- Standards: `.cursor/rules/karpathy-guidelines.mdc` and `.cursor/rules/ponytail.mdc` (both read) — bias toward minimal diffs, root-cause fixes, no speculative abstractions.
- Snapshot incomplete: false; manifest.json contains full inventory. Tests need not be executed; limitation must be disclosed in result.
- Verified facts so far:
  - `core/start.go`/`core/restart.go`: apply impairments per node only on the non-labruntime path; `startNodesWithLabRuntime`/`restartNodesWithLabRuntime` (k8s labruntime) do NOT apply impairments — potential coverage gap.
  - `links/link_brief.go` `ToTypeSpecificRawLink` rejects netem on brief host/macvlan/mgmt-net links (specialLinkTypes check inside endpoint loop), but extended forms (`type: host`, `type: macvlan`, `type: mgmt-net`, possibly others) appear to allow netem via shared `EndpointRaw` (`Netem *NetemRaw` yaml tag) — `LinkMacVlanRaw.Resolve` calls `r.Endpoint.Resolve(params, link)` so netem would be set/applied on non-veth endpoints, contradicting docs "Impairments are supported on veth links".
  - `GenericLinkNode.ExecFunction` does `ns.GetNS(g.nspath)` + `netns.Do(f)` — applies in root ns for host/bridge pseudo-nodes.
  - veth-stitch: `NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth` carries over `Endpoints` (including Netem), `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` redirects for SR-SIM etc. — netem likely propagates to node endpoints (probably OK).
  - Brief links: netem assignment logic in `linkVEthRawFromLinkBriefRaw` (≤2 netem entries); `ToLinkBriefRaw` on `LinkVEthRaw` appends netem list only if some endpoint has netem.
  - `netem/netem.go` unchanged: `NewTC(ns)`, `SetImpairments` (calls `ReplaceImpairments`, then finds qdisc), `ReplaceImpairments`, `DeleteImpairments`; `init()` calls `core.InitializeClock()`. Callers: `core/link_netem.go` uses `ReplaceImpairments`; `cmd/tools_netem.go` uses `SetImpairments`/`DeleteImpairments`.
  - Schema: `netem` ref added at lines ~1186 (brief link netem array) and ~1565 (`netem` definition in shared `link-endpoint`-like definition, description "Link impairment ... like containerlab tools netem set") — need to confirm which link-type definitions share that endpoint definition (whether non-veth extended types also accept netem).
  - `links/netem.go` validation: `maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond`, `maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64/1000`; jitter-without-delay error, loss 0–100 (NaN caught), rate overflow, corruption 0–100.
  - `links/netem_test.go` table-driven `TestNetemRawResolve` covers errors incl. "netem jitter must be at most 2.147483647s".
